ai.literal: If asked what is called old friendship, it is friendship that does not in any way breach the rights of intimacy.
ai.translation: If one asks what defines long-standing friendship, it is that friendship which never, in any way, destroys the mutual rights and liberties of intimacy.
ai.modern: பழைமை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எதுவென்றால், நண்பர்கள் தங்களுக்குள் இருக்கும் உரிமையை எக்காரணத்தைக் கொண்டும் சிதைக்காத நட்பாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essence of long-standing friendship (paḻaimai). The key word here is 'kiḻamai', which refers to the natural right, freedom, or ownership that close friends have over each other. True old friendship is characterized by 'kīḻntiṭā', meaning it does not breach or destroy this mutual liberty. Even when a friend takes liberties or acts without formal permission, the other does not take offense, preserving the deep bond of trust.

ai.literal: To friendship, the limb is intimate familiarity; and to that, being the seasoning salt is the duty of the noble.
ai.translation: Intimate familiarity is the very life-limb of friendship; to be the seasoning salt that makes this familiarity sweet is the duty of the noble.
ai.modern: நட்பிற்கு நெருங்கிய உரிமை பாராட்டுவதே சிறந்த உறுப்பாகும்; அந்த உரிமைக்கு இன்பம் தரும் உப்பாக விளங்குவது சான்றோரின் கடமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essence of long-standing friendship. The word 'keḻutakaimai' refers to the right of familiarity, where friends can act with freedom without needing formal permission. The poet states that this familiarity is the 'uṟuppu' (the vital limb or constituent) of friendship. To make this familiarity pleasant and enduring, noble friends must act as 'uppu' (salt or seasoning), gracefully accepting and returning this intimacy to keep the relationship flavorful and sweet.

ai.literal: Of what use will a long-standing friendship be, if one does not accept when a friend acts with intimate freedom accordingly?
ai.translation: Of what use is a long-standing friendship if one cannot graciously accept and accommodate a friend's actions done with the freedom of intimacy?
ai.modern: நண்பர்கள் உரிமை எடுத்துக்கொண்டு செய்யும் செயல்களை அப்படியே ஏற்றுக்கொண்டு உடன்படாதபோது, பழமையான நட்பினால் என்ன பயன் விளையும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core of long-standing friendship, which is the right to act with intimate freedom (keḻutakaimai) without fear of offending. If a person cannot happily accept and accommodate their friend's actions when they take such liberties, the long-standing friendship loses its value. The word 'keḻutakaimai' denotes the privilege of intimacy where formal permission is unnecessary. True friendship is proven not by mere duration, but by the capacity to tolerate and welcome the free, unconstrained actions of a close friend.

ai.literal: With a pleasing nature, desiringly they will remain, if, by the right of intimate friendship, without asking, friends do something.
ai.translation: If friends do something without asking, taking it as their right of intimacy, wise people will accept it lovingly, appreciating their desirable affection.
ai.modern: நெருங்கிய நண்பர்கள் நம்மிடம் கேட்காமலேயே ஒரு செயலைச் செய்தாலும், அதைத் தமக்குரிய உரிமையோடு செய்தார்கள் என்று கருதி, அன்புடையவர்கள் அதனை விரும்பி ஏற்றுக்கொள்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the beauty of deep, unquestioning friendship. When intimate friends take the liberty to act on our behalf without consulting us, we should not feel offended. Instead, we should view their action as a privilege of close friendship (கெழுதகைமை) and accept it with joy and affection (விழைதகையான் வேண்டி). True friendship transcends formal permissions, and accepting such actions strengthens the bond.

ai.literal: Is it merely folly? Great intimacy thus let one understand, if friends do things causing pain.
ai.translation: If friends do things that cause us pain, let us understand it not as mere folly, but as the privilege of great intimacy.
ai.modern: நண்பர்கள் நமக்குத் துன்பம் தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்தால், அதை அறியாமை என்று மட்டும் நினைக்காமல், அவர்கள் நம்மீது கொண்டுள்ள மிகுந்த உரிமை என்று உணர்ந்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet guides us on how to react when close friends act in ways that hurt us. The word 'கிழமை' means ownership, right, or deep intimacy. Instead of dismissing a friend's hurtful action as mere foolishness or ignorance (பேதைமை), we should view it as an exercise of their special right and freedom (பெருங்கிழமை) within the friendship. This perspective helps preserve long-standing relationships by replacing resentment with understanding.

ai.literal: Those who stood within the boundary of propriety will not abandon, even in times of ruin, the friendship of those who stood in long-standing affection.
ai.translation: Those who stand firm within the bounds of propriety will not abandon their relationship with long-standing friends, even in times of ruin.
ai.modern: நட்பின் எல்லையைக் கடக்காமல் வாழ்பவர்கள், தமக்கு அழிவு வந்த காலத்திலும், பழமையான நட்பில் நிலைத்து நின்றவர்களுடைய உறவைக் கைவிட மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the enduring nature of true friendship. The phrase 'எல்லைக்கண் நின்றார்' refers to principled individuals who never cross the boundaries of loyalty and proper conduct. 'தொல்லைக்கண் நின்றார்' refers to old, long-standing friends who have maintained their affection over a long period. The poet explains that even when facing complete ruin or adversity ('தொலைவிடத்தும்'), those of noble character will never abandon their ancient bonds, showing that historical loyalty is far more valuable than temporary material circumstances.

ai.literal: Even if they do things that bring ruin, they do not cut off their affection—those of friendship that came in the path of love.
ai.translation: Even if they do things that cause ruin or pain, those whose friendship has come down through long-standing affection will never diminish in their love.
ai.modern: அன்பின் வழியில் வந்த நீண்ட கால நட்பை உடையவர்கள், தமக்கு அழிவைத் தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்தாலும், அவர்கள் தம் அன்பைக் குறைத்துக் கொள்ள மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the strength of long-standing, traditional friendship. Those who share a deep-rooted friendship based on mutual affection will not abandon their love even if their friends commit acts that cause them ruin or distress. The key words 'அழிவந்த' (bringing ruin or pain) and 'அன்பறார்' (not cutting off love) emphasize that true, old friendship is resilient enough to withstand even severe mistakes or harmful actions.

ai.literal: To those capable of the intimate friendship of not hearing a friend's fault, if friends commit faults daily, [it is acceptable].
ai.translation: For those who possess the capability of intimate friendship that ignores a friend's faults, it is acceptable even if their friends commit lapses every single day.
ai.modern: நண்பர்களின் குற்றங்களைக் கேளாதவாறு கடந்துபோகும் நெருக்கமான நட்புரிமை கொண்டவர்களுக்கு, நண்பர்கள் நாள்தோறும் தவறுகளைச் செய்தாலும் அது குற்றமாகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the depth of true, long-standing friendship. The poet explains that those who have the rare capacity to overlook or ignore the faults of their close friends will not find it a problem even if those friends commit lapses every day. The word 'keḻutakaimai' refers to the right of intimacy where one does not take offense at a friend's actions. By 'kēḷā' (not hearing), the poet suggests deliberately ignoring or not paying attention to the shortcomings of loved ones to preserve the bond.

ai.translation: The world will cherish those who do not abandon the friendship of long-standing companions whose bond has come down through an unbroken lineage.

ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immense value of hereditary and long-standing friendship. The phrase 'keṭā-a vaḻivanta' describes a bond that has survived without decaying through generations. The poet states that the world highly esteems and loves those ('viṭā-ar') who remain loyal and refuse to abandon such deep-rooted relationships.

ai.literal: Those who do not love, to love they will be subjected, those who from proper behavior towards old friends do not deviate.
ai.translation: Those who never deviate from proper courtesy towards long-standing friends will be loved and cherished even by those who do not love them.
ai.modern: பழைய நண்பர்களிடம் காட்டும் அன்பான பண்பிலிருந்து விலகாமல் நடப்பவர்களை, அவர்களை விரும்பாத பகைவர்களும் விரும்பும் நிலை ஏற்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the power of maintaining long-standing relationships with courtesy and loyalty. The poet states that those who do not deviate from the proper code of conduct towards their old friends earn universal respect. Their steadfastness is so admirable that even strangers or enemies who previously did not care for them will come to love and desire their friendship. The key lies in preserving the intimacy of old friendships without overstepping boundaries or losing respect.
